title: Pen Test Coordination, Scope & Remediation Plan — RBAC v2 / Audit Logs / SIEM Export
body:
Purpose:
This doc coordinates an internal + third-party penetration test focused on our RBAC v2 rollout, the audit log schema and retention, automated evidence collection, and SIEM export coverage. Goal: validate that access controls are correct, that all privileged actions are logged with the required schema, that logs reliably export to our SIEM, and that we can generate a tamper-evident evidence package for compliance reviews.

High-level scope (in-scope):
- RBAC v2: role definitions, permission grants, role inheritance, and permission escalation paths across Console, API, and Dedicated/Private planes.
- Audit logs: event schema completeness (timestamp, actor, principal_type, resource_type, action, request_id, outcome, request_payload_hash, kv_cache_context), retention and immutability settings.
- Evidence automation: scripts and CI jobs that collect and package logs, signed manifests, sample replay traces.
- SIEM export: delivery pipeline to Splunk/Elastic/Datadog, field mappings, missing-field detection, delivery failure handling.

Out of scope (for this engagement):
- Full application code security review (separate SAST/DAST required).
- On-prem hardware threat modelling.

Timeline and milestones:
- 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting (internal + vendor) — review scope and rules of engagement.
- 2026-03-09: Staging environment baseline checks (RBAC v2 deployed, audit agents enabled).
- 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-20: Active testing window (black/grey box as agreed).
- 2026-03-24: Draft findings due from vendor.
- 2026-04-07: Internal remediation plan due (owners assigned).
- 2026-04-21: Vendor verification re-test.

Primary contacts & roles:
- Executive sponsor: Asha Kapoor (Head of Security) — escalation and approval.
- Project owner: Rachel Kim (Security Engineering) — coordination, ticketing, evidence collector.
- RBAC SME: Omar Patel (Platform Engineering).
- Logging & SIEM SME: Sofia Martinez (Observability).
- Evidence automation & infra: Ethan Brooks (DevOps).
- External vendor: RedTeam Labs (point: tbd).

Pre-test checklist (must be completed before 2026-03-09):
- RBAC test accounts created with well-labelled tags (pen-test/role-*) and expiration set to test window end. Owner: Omar.
- Service-account audit log toggles verified: all service-account actions are logged. Owner: Sofia.
- Audit log retention policy set to 1 year in staging; write-once storage (S3 object lock / GCS retention) enabled for evidence bucket. Owner: Ethan.
- SIEM export pipeline enabled in staging and verified using synthetic events. Owner: Sofia.
- Evidence automation repo branch (evidence/pen-test-2026) created and CI job configured to: collect logs, generate manifest (SHA256), sign manifest with KMS key, upload to evidence bucket. Owner: Ethan.

Audit log schema (required fields and examples):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC (2026-03-16T14:12:05Z)
- event_id: UUID v4
- request_id: opaque request id propagated across services (redwood-req-...)
- actor_id: princ: user|service/<id>
- actor_role: canonical role name at time of action (e.g., admin.readonly, infra.deployer)
- principal_type: user | service_account | session_token
- resource_type: model | route | deployment | credential | key
- resource_id: canonical resource identifier (deployment: dply-1234)
- action: verb (create, update, delete, grant_role, assume_role, get_secret)
- outcome: success | failure | denied | error
- client_ip: IP address (if applicable)
- user_agent: SDK/Console/Tool name and version
- request_payload_hash: SHA256 of payload (optional for privacy but required for evidence integrity checks)
- kv_cache_context: optional context string for cache hits/misses when serving runtime operations are exercised
- resolver_trace_id: optional trace id linking to distributed trace for replay

Schema enforcement rules for the test:
- Events that touch privileged resources (role changes, key access, deployment scaling, secret read) must include request_payload_hash and actor_role.
- Missing required fields in >1% of privileged events will be flagged as a medium finding.

Evidence automation plan (artifact expectations):
- Evidence package format: gzipped folder with 3 files: logs.jsonl.gz, manifest.json (SHA256 list), signature.sig (KMS-signed manifest).
- Naming convention: redwood-pen-test-2026-<env>-<YYYYMMDD>-<vendor>.tar.gz
- Collection window: test start minus 1 hour to test end plus 1 hour.
- Storage: evidence-redwood-locked (S3) with object-lock enabled and access limited to security/evidence service account.
- CI job steps (high-level):
  1) Triggered manually by project owner.
  2) Use log-export API to pull events matching request_id prefixes assigned to pen-test accounts.
  3) Aggregate into logs.jsonl with canonical schema.
  4) Generate manifest.json: list of files + SHA256 + min/max timestamp.
  5) Sign manifest with KMS asymmetric key.
  6) Upload package to evidence bucket and emit signed URL to slack:#sec-pen-tests.

SIEM export and field mapping (checks for test):
- Verify field mapping: event_id -> id, timestamp -> @timestamp, actor_role -> user.role, resource_type -> object.type, action -> event.action, outcome -> event.outcome, request_payload_hash -> event.data.hash.
- Verify parse rules handle nested JSON payloads and base64 encoded payloads.
- Ensure alert rule coverage: failed attempts to change roles, privilege grants to external emails, sudden creation of long-lived keys, anomalous access from new IP ranges.
- Delivery guarantees: at least 99.9% of events within the 2-hour window must be present in SIEM for length of test. Missing or delayed exports must be logged and included in evidence with S3/Exporter error logs.

Findings triage & remediation workflow (for vendor findings):
- Vendor publishes a draft report with severity tags (critical/high/medium/low) and reproducible steps including request_id/time windows.
- Security owner (Rachel) creates a parent JIRA (JIRA-SEC-####) and one child ticket per finding. Child ticket template fields: title, severity, reproduction steps, affected env, proposed mitigation, owner, target fix date, verification steps.
- Owners submit code/config PRs (link in ticket) and mark ticket in progress.
- For RBAC misconfigurations: preferred fix is to change role binding to least privilege and add a unit/regression test that checks role coverage & denies unintended permission.
- For missing audit fields: patch logging library and add schema validator in log ingestion pipeline; create migration to backfill missing fields where feasible.
- For SIEM gaps: add mapping rules and pipeline tests; if exporter dropped events due to throttling, increase buffer/throughput or implement durable delivery.

Example finding (illustrative):
- Title: "role-inheritance allows infra.deployer to grant admin.readonly"
- Severity: high
- Repro steps: use pen-test account role-deployer to call /grant_role with target=admin.readonly; observe success; request_id: redwood-req-xxxx; see audit event with outcome=success.
- Immediate remediation: remove grant permission from infra.deployer and rotate any keys used during test.
- Full remediation: update role graph to prevent lateral privilege grant, add regression test and policy-enforcement check in CI, schedule RBAC policy review.
- Verification: vendor re-test and provide request_id showing denied outcome.

Verification & acceptance criteria:
- All critical findings must be remediated and vendor-verified within 30 days of the final report.
- High findings: remediated or mitigated and verified within 60 days.
- Medium/low: tracked and justified with business risk acceptance if not remediated.
- Evidence package must contain signed manifest and raw logs matching vendor repro steps for verified findings.

Post-test deliverables from vendor (required):
- Draft findings report (with request_id/time windows and reproduction steps).
- Final findings report after 7 business days post-discussion.
- Signed attestation that no persistent test agents were left in environments.
- Re-test verification for fixed critical/high items.

Appendix A — quick commands and queries:
- Pull events by request id prefix (example pseudo-API):
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' "https://logs.internal.redwood/v1/exports?start=2026-03-16T13:00:00Z&end=2026-03-20T23:00:00Z&request_id_prefix=redwood-pen-" | gzip > logs.jsonl.gz

- Splunk/KQL example to surface privilege grants:
  index=redwood_logs event.action="grant_role" | table _time, actor_id, actor_role, resource_id, outcome, request_id

- SIEM KQL to find missing fields:
  where isnull(actor_role) or isnull(request_payload_hash) | summarize count() by event.action

Appendix B — evidence naming & retention policy reminders:
- Evidence bucket lifecycle: objects with prefix redwood-pen-test-2026/* -> 365d retention, immutability = on.
- Access: read-only to security/audit and vendor ephemeral read access via signed URL for 7 days.

Open questions to resolve in kickoff:
- Vendor scope: are social engineering phishing tests included? (We suggest no.)
- Will vendor be allowed to attempt exploit attempts against Dedicated/Private infra that might cause service impact? Need explicit approval and blast-radius limits.
- KMS key for signing: which key ring/account should be used for vendor-signed manifests?

Next steps (action items):
- Rachel: schedule kickoff meeting and publish this doc to confluence (CONFLUENCE-7894) by 2026-02-20.
- Omar: prepare RBAC attack surface list and test account role mappings by 2026-02-27.
- Sofia: run SIEM synthetic event test and post result to slack by 2026-02-25.
- Ethan: create evidence automation branch and CI job skeleton by 2026-02-28.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working coordination doc. Expect iterative updates and additional technical appendices (log samples, role graphs) to be attached as separate files in the evidence repo.
